## Natural history notes

A medium-sized paper wasp characterized by its slender reddish-brown to dark body, long dangling legs, smoky wings, and narrow waist, with yellow markings that are usually less extensive than in some other paper wasps. In Florida, it is found in gardens, fields, forest edges, parks, yards, buildings, and other open or semi-open habitats where sheltered sites are available for nesting. It builds open, umbrella-shaped paper nests from chewed plant fibers, and adults hunt caterpillars and other soft-bodied insects to feed their larvae while also visiting flowers for nectar.
